title: Marguerite and the Trail
premise: Salvage diver Edmund Quintana is pulling artifacts from a wrecked naval transport off a monsoon-battered coast when a government survey team vanishes onshore, leaving their gear arranged in a perfect line pointing inland — a trail only someone who knew the wreck's true cargo could follow. Joined by his estranged sister Marguerite, who arrives claiming half of everything their missing father left him, including the compass that doesn't point north, Edmund follows the trail to a hidden cache of war-era gold that the vanished surveyors were secretly cataloguing for men above their pay grade. Hunted by the contractors sent to erase the evidence, the siblings must survive the monsoon, expose the cover-up through the one surviving surveyor, and choose between selling the inheritance or returning it to the coastal families it was stolen from decades ago.
about_author: B. M. Coldharbour is the pen name of a former maritime archivist who spent six years cataloguing declassified salvage reports before turning to fiction. They write from a houseboat on an unnamed estuary, where the tide dictates both the writing schedule and the mood.

chapters.title: The Wreck Nobody Names
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Diving the forbidden wreck, Edmund recovers a sealed strongbox stamped with a government mark he's seen once before — on his dead father's effects. His boat, the Marguerite, takes hull damage from a patrol vessel's wake. Emotional beat: unease hardening into resolve; he decides not to report the find.

chapters.title: A Sister with Half a Claim
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Marguerite arrives at the harbor with their father's letters and a lawyer's letter of her own, demanding her share of the estate — including the brass compass Edmund wears around his neck. Their argument is interrupted by news: the navy survey team stationed upcoast has vanished overnight. Emotional beat: old resentment cracking into reluctant alliance.

chapters.title: Gear Without Tracks
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. The siblings reach the abandoned survey camp: instruments laid out in a precise line inland, food untouched, no footprints after a rain that should have recorded everything. Edmund recognizes the arrangement as a signal — a diver's line-and-bearing drill. Emotional beat: dread; someone wanted the trail found by exactly the right person.

chapters.title: What the Compass Wants
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Following the trail inland, Marguerite notices the compass needle pulls off north whenever Edmund leads. She confronts him: their father used this compass on the same coast thirty years ago. Flashback fragments reveal he was part of the original salvage operation. Emotional beat: betrayal curdling into curiosity.

chapters.title: The Man in the Mangroves
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. They find Devi Raghunathan, the sole surviving surveyor, hiding wounded in the mangrove swamp. He confesses the team discovered a gold cache looted from coastal villages during the war, and that his employers ordered the evidence — and the team — erased. Emotional beat: guilt transformed into purpose; Devi becomes their witness.

chapters.title: Contractors at High Water
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. The contractors reach the coast; the siblings' escape downriver fails when the Marguerite's patched hull splits. Trapped in a stilt village as the monsoon peaks, they bargain with villagers whose grandparents lost everything to the original looting. Emotional beat: fear giving way to solidarity; the inheritance stops being abstract.

chapters.title: The Cache Below
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Using the compass and his father's letters, Edmund dives a flooded sinkhole connected to the sea cave and finds the cache — and proof his father hid it there deliberately, waiting for someone to finish what he couldn't. Contractors arrive at the sinkhole rim. Emotional beat: grief and pride entwined; Edmund understands his inheritance at last.

chapters.title: Monsoon Reckoning
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Climax begins: the contractors take Devi hostage and demand the cache coordinates. Marguerite trades herself for Devi, buying Edmund time to rig the collapsing sinkhole. Rising tension peaks as the storm surge turns the cave system into a trap for pursuers and treasure alike. Emotional beat: courage she didn't know she'd inherited.

chapters.title: Everything the Water Keeps
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Climax resolves: Edmund floods the cache chamber, drowning the gold and nearly himself, while Marguerite's recording of Devi's testimony transmits to a journalist anchored offshore. The contractors are caught by the surge and by the evidence. Emotional beat: sacrifice without martyrdom; justice achieved outside any courtroom.

chapters.title: Marguerite and the Trail
chapters.summary: Shared POV, alternating. Weeks later, the inquiry opens, the villages file their claims, and the siblings repair the boat together. The compass, its work done, finally points true north. Marguerite signs on as co-owner; the debt between them dissolves into partnership. Emotional beat: quiet resolution — the real inheritance was each other and the truth.
